title: Use validated utility calls for implicitly convertible arguments in GDScript
body:

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Related to #85514

## Additional information

<!--
Provide additional information and explanation of your PR, including areas that you are uncertain of or require special attention from reviewers. For examples, please read our pull request guidelines: https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#explain-your-contributions
-->

Utility function validated calls will do `VariantCaster::cast` internally, so arg types do not need to match the signature exactly to be able to use validated path. This PR relaxes the condition to implicitly convertiable (`Variant::can_convert_strict`), which means calls like `sin(int)` now use the validated path.

<details>
<summary>benchmark</summary>

`scons production=yes scu_build=yes tests=yes`

<details>
<summary>code</summary>

```gdscript
extends Node2D

const OUTER_LOOPS = 10
const INNER_LOOPS = 1000000

func _ready():
	for i in OUTER_LOOPS:
		print("\n%s:" % i)

		var start : int
		var end : int

		start = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		for j in INNER_LOOPS:
			var ret : float = sin(j)
			#assert(ret == sin(float(j)))
		end = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		print(end - start, " us")
		
		start = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		for j in INNER_LOOPS:
			var ret : float = sin(float(j))
		end = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		print(end - start, " us")
		
		start = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		for j in INNER_LOOPS:
			var ret : Vector2 = Vector2.from_angle(j)
		end = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		print(end - start, " us")
```
</details>
